title: RemoteTransform3D will drift scale very slowly when "Update Scale" is _unchecked_.
body: ### Tested versions 4.5 & 4.6 ### System information Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7216) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads) - 63.78 GiB memory ### Issue description I have RemoteTransform3D nodes attached to a Skeleton with animations on it. The animations make lots of small rotations in a loop. It has "Update Global", "Update Position" and importantly, "Update Remote" checked while "Update Scale" is _unchecked_. The object RemoteTransform3D is updating will very slowly drift its scale away from [1,1,1] over time due to very small floating point precision error accumulation from the rotation-without-scale. ### Steps to reproduce Create a remote transform that rotates a cube without updating scale. Results: - Over about 5-10 minutes you will see very small errors accumulate on the target object: Expectation: the target objects scale should remain fixed over time. This will eventually trigger endless error warnings in the console from Jolt if the target object is a collision object or contains a collision object. Each axis will drift ever so slightly and when they are far enough off the error check will start logging. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
